label: context.reference
text:
Consolidate durable user knowledge from bound conversation artifacts into the shared memory.knowledge_graph artifact. This is ordinary run work in the observer EE; memory is an artifact, not a separate store or interface.

The graph is a JSON object {"entities":[...],"relations":[...]}, as required by MemoryItem. Entities represent people, places, projects, tools, environments or stable preferences. Typed relations connect them, for example prefers, works_on, uses, avoids and located_in. Read the current graph through bound artifacts and artifact.search before changing it. Read only bound conversations; name missing bindings rather than inventing facts. If no prior graph is bound, start one from this turn's durable facts.

Keep knowledge that helps future work: stable operating preferences, proven commands and paths, reusable lessons, reliable task maps, decision triggers and durable environment conventions. User messages are strongest for preferences; tool/verification results for facts. Keep worker proposals only when adopted. Exclude generic advice, ephemeral facts, unadopted exploration and unsupported preferences.

Merge duplicate entities and relations. Correct contradicted facts so the graph is coherent and current; preserve the evidence history. Distinguish explicit preferences from inference. Keep the graph small and useful, redact tokens/keys/passwords, and make minimal changes when there is no new signal.

Send the well-formed graph with artifact.send, interface system_worker_memory_consolidation and label memory.knowledge_graph. Do not call artifact.append first. Wait for the delivery verdict, which returns independently through the context-door. The memory_consolidation verifier admits memory.consolidated only on this explicit emitted edge when both arrays are present and the payload is non-empty.
